result.rationale: The new refreshOAuthTokens helper performs fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... }) with no AbortSignal or timeout, and this helper is wired into the token-refresh paths of Google, Office365, Zoom, Webex, Lark, Zoho, and Hubspot calendar/video services shown in the diff. This is a true, specific, decision-relevant reliability concern about newly added code, but the absence of an explicit timeout on an external fetch is not strictly incorrect behavior

judged_text: The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no AbortSignal timeout, so a hung parent sync endpoint stalls the token-refresh path with no bound. Calendar availability and booking operations that need a token refresh block for up to the platform's default idle timeouts (minutes) per call whenever the parent cal.com endpoint is slow or down, turning a remote outage into local request stalls on the booking path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, performs `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: ... })` without any timeout/`AbortSignal` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple calendar/video services now await this call during token refresh (e.g., Google/Office365/Zoom/Webex/etc.), so a slow/hung sync endpoint can stall request handling. This is a concrete resilience/performance concern grounded in the diff, though not a strictly incorrect behavior in terms of functional correctness.
